data.name: Freestyle 2: Street Basketball
data.detailed_description:
Freestyle 2 is the Ultimate Online Street Basketball Game!

  • Experience a superior gameplay of basketball and perform freestyle street basketball moves!

  • Enjoy the excitement of vibrant street basketball with its unique cel-shaded graphics and game experience.

One Player, One Character

  • Pick a character based on their position move up in the league.

  • Choose the progression depending on your favorite play style.

  • Test your teamwork with other basketball players online and show’em what you got!

Key Features

  • Positions: Center, Power Forward, Small Forward, Shooting Guard, Point Guard, Control Tower, Dual Guard, Swing Man.

  • Skills: Create your own play style with over 30 moves including shooting and passing skills!

  • Tournament & Crew: Team up with your crewmates and win in a tournament for a chance at great items and prizes!

  • Customization: Customize your character’s look. Choose from a wide range of outfits, hairstyles, shoes, accessories to make your own fashion statement!

  • Tutorial & Training: Exclusive tutorials on how to execute each and every skill in the game.

reviews.review:
My Honest Review of This Game: Pay-to-Win, Toxicity, and Cheating

I have been playing this game since it was first released on North American servers, and I genuinely loved it at first. The basketball mechanics felt fresh and different from the typical NBA 2K games, which made the experience unique and exciting.

Unfortunately, over time, the game's major problems have become increasingly difficult to ignore. Despite its potential, several issues continue to hold it back.

1. THIS GAME IS PAY-TO-WIN!

Ever since paywalls became a major part of the game, competing at a professional level without spending money has become increasingly difficult. In my experience, players may need to spend at least $50 to have a competitive advantage.

Special characters often come with incredibly strong attributes and abilities that free-to-play players cannot easily match. Clothing and cosmetic items can also provide additional stats, meaning that even customization can contribute to a competitive advantage.

To give credit where it is due, JOYCITY has made efforts to help free-to-play players by giving away characters, VC, and other useful items. These changes are appreciated, especially for players who do not want to spend money.

However, giving away free rewards does not eliminate the underlying problem. There is still a substantial difference between a free-to-play player and someone willing to spend heavily on the game. When money can significantly influence your ability to compete, it becomes difficult to argue that the game offers a fair playing field.

2. THE LEARNING CURVE IS MOUNT EVEREST!

This game has an enormous learning curve, and the difference between an inexperienced player and a highly skilled player can be ridiculous.

There are so many mechanics, skills, character attributes, matchups, and meta strategies to learn that mastering one position is already a major commitment. I have spent approximately 600 hours learning how to play Center, and I still barely know how to play the other positions at a high level. Learning those roles would require a substantial additional time investment.

The problem is not that a competitive game requires skill. Skill-based gameplay is one of the things that makes a game rewarding. The problem is how overwhelming the learning process can become for new players.

New players are expected to understand complicated mechanics and strategies while competing against experienced players who know how to exploit every weakness. Without proper guidance or a more welcoming learning environment, it is easy to see why newcomers would become frustrated and quit.

A game can have a high skill ceiling without making the entry-level experience miserable.

3. THE COMMUNITY IS HORRIBLE!

The community can be incredibly toxic, especially toward players who do not understand their roles or know every meta strategy.

If you make mistakes, miss an assignment, or fail to perform at a professional level, you can find yourself dealing with harassment, insults, and constant trash talk from teammates.

I will admit that I have been part of this problem myself. When matches become so competitive that every mistake can cost the entire game, frustration builds quickly. At higher levels, players are expected to perform consistently, and even small mistakes can be punished by an organized team.

However, that does not excuse the toxicity. The game's unforgiving competitive environment can encourage players to blame their teammates instead of helping them improve.

The result is a frustrating cycle: experienced players demand perfection, inexperienced players struggle to keep up, and new players are driven away before they have a chance to learn.

If the game wants to maintain a healthy player base, it needs an environment where players can improve without being constantly ridiculed.

4. CHEATERS ARE RUINING THE COMPETITIVE EXPERIENCE!

Another major problem is cheating. Encounters with suspected lag switchers, players who appear to teleport across the court because of abnormal lag, and alleged automatic green-release cheats can make competitive matches feel unfair.

When someone appears to gain an advantage through exploits or unauthorized tools rather than skill, it undermines the entire purpose of competitive play.

There is nothing more frustrating than spending hundreds of hours learning your position, improving your timing, and understanding the game's mechanics, only to encounter opponents who appear to bypass those mechanics entirely.

Of course, unusual lag does not automatically prove that someone is cheating. However, recurring suspicious behaviour and inadequate responses to confirmed cheating can seriously damage players' trust in the competitive environment.

JOYCITY needs to take cheating reports seriously, improve detection and enforcement, and communicate more clearly about its efforts to protect fair play.

FINAL THOUGHTS

I genuinely love the foundation of this game. Its basketball mechanics offer something different from the traditional NBA 2K experience, and that uniqueness is what kept me playing for so long.

But a great concept cannot carry a game forever when monetization, an overwhelming learning curve, community toxicity, and cheating continue to undermine the experience.

JOYCITY deserves credit for providing free characters, VC, and other rewards to its player base. However, more needs to be done to create a fair competitive environment, help newcomers learn the game, discourage toxic behaviour, and protect legitimate players from cheaters.

I want this game to succeed. That is precisely why these problems are so frustrating. After investing hundreds of hours into learning and enjoying the game, it is disappointing to see its potential held back by issues that make the experience less accessible and less rewarding.

This game has the potential to be something special, but until these problems are addressed, it will continue to push away the very players who want to see it thrive.
